To fix (5)

To fix Exact P-Values

What we found

We found 1 imprecise p value out of 25 detected p values.

Show details

Reporting p values imprecisely (e.g., p < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in p value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., p = .032) unless p values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use p < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., “decreased at the p < .05 significance threshold”).

P-Value Text
p < 0.0083 Double asterisks (**) indicate significance after Bonferroni correction: p < 0.000416 (corrected for 120 independent tests) for the birth cohort analyses and at p < 0.0083 (corrected for 6 independent tests) for the generation analyses.

The APA manual states: Report exact p values (e.g., p = .031) to two or three decimal places. However, report p values less than .001 as p < .001. However, 2 decimals is too imprecise for many use-cases (e.g., a p value meta-analysis), so report p values with three digits.

American Psychological Association (2020). Publication manual of the American Psychological Association, 7 edition. American Psychological Association.

Unclassified Files

We could not classify 1 file by name or extension: run_weightedLD_susie_metal_array.slurm. Add a recognisable keyword (data, code, materials, documentation, output) to the file name, or use a common extension, so both humans and machines can tell what kind of file it is.

Files that do not belong in the repository

We left out 2 files that software creates by itself, not the authors: R history (2). They hold nothing a reader can use, but they clutter the repository, and software can mistake them for real files (for example a ._ copy of a .csv for data).

Remove these: Operating system files: macOS adds a __MACOSX folder and a ._ copy of every file it puts in a zip, and .DS_Store files to folders; Windows adds Thumbs.db and desktop.ini. On a Mac, create zips from the command line with zip -r -X, or remove them afterwards with zip -d archive.zip "__MACOSX/*" "*.DS_Store". RStudio session files (.Rproj.user/) hold open tabs and unsaved edits; R history (.Rhistory) lists the commands typed in a session and can hold file paths and passwords; Jupyter checkpoints (.ipynb_checkpoints/) are automatic copies of notebooks; compiled Python files (__pycache__/, .pyc) are recreated when the code runs; open-document lock files (~$...docx, .~lock...#) are left while a document is open; editor backups (file~, .bak, .swp) and temporary files (.tmp, .temp) are copies a program made by itself.

Keep only on purpose: version control folders (.git, .svn, .hg) hold the project’s history, which can include earlier versions of files and data that was later removed; editor settings (.idea, .vscode) can hold paths on your own computer. A .gitignore based on GitHub’s templates (https://github.com/github/gitignore) keeps them out of a repository.

This module runs automated data-quality checks (empty columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, stray whitespace, numbers stored as text, problematic and colliding column names, mixed text encodings, personal information, spreadsheet formatting, and careless responding) on the extracted data files.

We examined 5 columns across 2 data files.

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 2 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. setwd() calls were found in 5 code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). No install.packages() calls were found in any of the code files.

Libraries / Imports

Best programming practice is to load all required libraries/imports in one block near the top of the code. In 12 code files, libraries/imports were at multiple places (i.e., with more than 3 non-comment lines in between).

How to make your code run on another computer

We ran your code on a clean computer, the way a reader or reviewer would. Below is each problem we found, the scripts it affects, and how to fix it. Fix them in the order given: a problem near the top can cause the ones below it.

Files are missing from your deposit.

  • upset.R reads locus_level_highPIP_patterns_core_priority.tsv.

The script stops at the line that reads the file.

  1. Find the file on your computer.
  2. Add it to the deposit, in the folder where the script looks for it.
  3. If you cannot share it, for example for privacy reasons, say so in the README, and explain where readers can get it and where to put it.

A script uses a location that exists only on your computer.

  • European_Heritability_Tables_Figures.r reads /YOUR PATH HERE/european/CLEAN/GWAS_QC/Heritability/raw/ever_tobacco_user_h2_raw.log.

No other computer has that folder, and the file is also not in the deposit.

  1. Add the file to the deposit.
  2. In the script, write the location from the top folder of your project, such as data/survey.csv. In R, here::here(“data”, “survey.csv”) does this for you.
  3. Remove any setwd() lines.

A package could not be installed.

  • Smoking_Initiation_European_AR1_Model_generation_additional.r needs TwoSampleMR.
  • Smoking_Initiation_European_AR1_Model_generation.r needs TwoSampleMR.

TwoSampleMR could not be installed with the current version of R, probably because it is old. Record the versions you used (in R, renv::init() writes them to a renv.lock file) and your R version. To be sure the code keeps running, provide a Docker image: a frozen copy of the whole computer setup the code needs, which you can build from rocker/r-ver at your R version.

A script starts a program outside R or Python.

  • Age_Trajectories_ModeratedEffect_8_Birthyear_Bin4_19.r starts /YOUR.
  • Meta_Analysis_METAL_cross-ancestryMA_generation13_ExploreResults_locuszoom.r starts /YOUR.
  • Meta_Analysis_METAL_cross-ancestryMA_generation14_ExploreResults_locuszoom.r starts /YOUR.
  • Meta_Analysis_METAL_cross-ancestry_birthyear_to16bins_ExploreResults.r starts /YOUR.
  • Meta_Analysis_METAL_cross-ancestryMA_generation24_ExploreResults_locuszoom.r starts /YOUR.
  • Age_Trajectories_MainEffect_1670_Birthyear_Bin4_19.r starts /YOUR.
  • AfricanAmerican_Clean_DAT_full.r starts /YOUR.
  • AfricanAmerican_Clean_passedQC_SNP_birthyear.r starts /YOUR.
  • AfricanAmerican_Clean_passedQC_SNP_gender.r starts /YOUR.
  • AfricanAmerican_Clean_passedQC_SNP_region.r starts /YOUR.
  • and 36 more

Our computer does not have this program, and neither will most readers’. Name the program, its version and where to get it in the README. A Docker image can include it.

A script uses something it does not create or load itself.

  • European_Genetic_Correlation_23andmeSI_Tables_Figures.r: Gender1
  • European_Genetic_Correlation_Tables_Figures.r: Trait1
  • Popcorn_Figure_creation.r: moderator

Usually the object was still in your R session from earlier work, or another script made it.

  1. Restart R (in RStudio: Session > Restart R).
  2. Run each script from top to bottom, and fix what is missing.
  3. If a script needs results of another, save them to a file in the first script and read them in the second.
  4. Load every package with library() at the top.

A script runs longer than our limit of 5 minutes.

  • survivalSim.R

State in the README how long each script runs. If some steps take hours, save their results (such as fitted models) to files, add those to the deposit, and let the script read them, so readers can check the rest without waiting.

A script waits for a person to choose a file, answer a question, or give arguments on the command line.

Nobody can answer when the code is checked automatically. Write the file name into the script, and put the exact command with its arguments in the README.

Comparison with the paper

Of the 17 statistical tests reported in the paper, 0 were found in the output of the code. No script ran to the end, so most results were never produced.

All details of the Reproducibility Check

This module assesses whether the paper’s code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 55 R code files.

Run order

A dependency cycle was detected among 12 files (AfricanAmerican_Clean_DAT_birthyear.r, AfricanAmerican_Clean_DAT_gender.r, AfricanAmerican_Clean_DAT_region.r, EastAsian_Clean_DAT_birthyear.r, EastAsian_Clean_DAT_gender.r, EastAsian_Clean_DAT_region.r, European_Clean_DAT_birthyear.r, European_Clean_DAT_gender.r, European_Clean_DAT_region.r, Latino_Clean_DAT_birthyear.r, Latino_Clean_DAT_gender.r, Latino_Clean_DAT_region.r): each reads a file another writes, so no run order satisfies all of them. This must be resolved before the code can run.

File paths

Every data path in the code works in the repository as deposited. 2 data paths were built at runtime with sprintf()/paste()/file.path() instead of written as a literal path — this is fragile authoring practice (it silently breaks if the code is run from a different working directory than the author’s own). We resolved all of these on a best-effort basis.

Files the deposit does not hold

The scripts that did not run through read 1 data file that is not in the deposit, and no script of the deposit writes: locus_level_highpip_patterns_core_priority.tsv.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 55 scripts: 0 ran without error, 51 errored, 1 timed out, 2 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions. 1 script needs a person to choose a file, answer a question or use an app, which cannot be reproduced without one: run_susie_metal_weighted_ld_one_locus.R. Naming the file in the script solves this.

Undefined-variable errors

3 scripts failed on an undefined variable or function (object '...' not found / could not find function "..."). This typically means the script expects a variable or function that another script defines — i.e. it is meant to be sourced into a larger session, not run on its own — or the symbol is simply never created. When another of the paper’s own script files defines the same name, this is called out below as a likely sourcing/copy-paste gap. Each is counted as an error (red).

File Missing variable Defined in
European_Genetic_Correlation_23andmeSI_Tables_Figures.r Gender1 (not defined anywhere in the paper’s code)
European_Genetic_Correlation_Tables_Figures.r Trait1 (not defined anywhere in the paper’s code)
Popcorn_Figure_creation.r moderator (not defined anywhere in the paper’s code)

Dependency-unavailable errors

2 scripts could not run because their own dependency is unavailable — the package failed to install from both live CRAN and the CRAN Archive (or a GitHub/URL source could not be resolved). This is an infrastructure limitation, not a defect in the paper’s code, so it does not force the traffic light red.

File
Smoking_Initiation_European_AR1_Model_generation_additional.r
Smoking_Initiation_European_AR1_Model_generation.r

setwd() in the code

5 scripts call setwd(). This is bad practice: it hardcodes where the code must run (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine) and breaks the moment the code is run anywhere else. To run the code we replaced these calls with a statement that does nothing. Any such script that then ran is reproducible only after ignoring a setwd() that should not have been in the code and needs to be fixed.

File setwd() removed Path(s) it set

European_Genetic_Correlation_Tables_Figures.r 11 (non-literal)
European_Genetic_Correlation_23andmeSI_Tables_Figures.r 5 (non-literal)
Smoking_Initiation_European_AR1_Model_generation.r 1 (non-literal)
Smoking_Initiation_European_AR1_Model_generation_additional.r 1 (non-literal)

Calls that install packages in the code

23 calls to install.packages(), groundhog, checkpoint, renv, pacman and the like were replaced, since they install packages themselves: groundhog.library() and p_load() by library(), the others by a statement that does nothing. The scripts ran with the packages installed before the run.

> restructure_sumstats_subgroups <- function(sub, dir) {
>   for (SUBGROUP in sub) {
>     cat(paste0("\n*----------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP, " --------------------------------*\n"))
>     data_name <- paste0("sumstats_", SUBGROUP)

> 
>     # keep certain columns in [sumstat_SUBGROUP]
>     cat("\nkeep certain columns in [sumstat_SUBGROUP].\n")
>     assign(data_name_new, subset(get(data_name), select=c("all.data.id", "src", "log.p", "effect", "stderr", 
>                                                           "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con", "pass",
>                                                           "freq.a0", "freq.a1", "freq.b0", "freq.b1",
>                                                           "freq.a", "freq.b", "MAF")), envir = .GlobalEnv)
>     print(head(get(data_name_new),n=5))
>     print(dim(get(data_name_new)))
>     # remove original data to save space  
>     rm(list = data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
> 
>     # merge [sumstat_SUBGROUP_subset] and [snp_all_merged_subset] using "all.data.id"
>     cat("\nmerge [sumstat_SUBGROUP_subset] and [snp_all_merged_subset] using all.data.id.\n")

>     print(tail(merged, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged))
> 
>     #Remove 'chr' from 'scaffold'.

>     print(tail(merged_chr_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_chr_CLEAN))

>                                mutate(
>                                       A=substr(alleles,1,1), #first character
>                                       B=substr(alleles,nchar(alleles),nchar(alleles)) #last character
>                                       ) #mutate
>     print(head(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN, n=5))

>     print(head(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN, n=5))

>     print(dim(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN))
>

>                               "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con",
>                               "freq.a0", "freq.a1", "freq.b0", "freq.b1",
>                               "freq.a", "freq.b", "MAF",
>                               "im.freq.a", "im.freq.b", "avg.rsqr", "min.rsqr", 
>                               "gt.rate", "gt.freq.a", "gt.freq.b")
> 
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN1))
> 
>    ##-----------------------------------

> 
>     #Keep 'chr1-22' only.

> metaanalysis_sumstats_subgroups <- function(sub, dir) {
>   for (SUBGROUP in sub) {
>     cat(paste0("\n*----------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP, " --------------------------------*\n"))

>                             ) #ifelse
>     ### case
>     sumstats$N_B1 <- NA  # initialize
>     sumstats$N_B1 <- ifelse(

>                             ) #ifelse
>

>     sumstats$N_0 <- NA  # initialize

>                             ) #ifelse

>                             ) #ifelse
> 
>     ## frequency of A allele ([freq.a0] and [freq.a1])
>     ### control
>     sumstats$freq.a0 <- NA  # initialize

> restructure_sumstats_subgroups <- function(sub, dir) {
>   for (SUBGROUP in sub) {
>     cat(paste0("\n*----------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP, " --------------------------------*\n"))
>     data_name <- paste0("sumstats_", SUBGROUP)
>     data_name_new <- paste0("sumstats_", SUBGROUP, "_subset")
> 
>     # keep certain columns in [sumstat_SUBGROUP]
>     cat("\nkeep certain columns in [sumstat_SUBGROUP].\n")
>     assign(data_name_new, subset(get(data_name), select=c("all.data.id", "src", "log.p", "effect", "stderr", 
>                                                           "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con", "pass",
>                                                           "freq.a0", "freq.a1", "freq.b0", "freq.b1",
>                                                           "freq.a", "freq.b", "MAF")), envir = .GlobalEnv)
>     print(head(get(data_name_new),n=5))
>     print(dim(get(data_name_new)))
>     # remove original data to save space  
>     rm(list = data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
> 
>     # merge [sumstat_SUBGROUP_subset] and [snp_all_merged_subset] using "all.data.id"
>     cat("\nmerge [sumstat_SUBGROUP_subset] and [snp_all_merged_subset] using all.data.id.\n")
>     merged <- merge(get(data_name_new), snp_all_merged_subset, by="all.data.id") # I do not specify "all=T" as I only need the matching SNP.
>     print(head(merged, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged))
> 
>     #Remove 'chr' from 'scaffold'.
>     cat("\nRemove 'chr' from 'scaffold'.\n")
>     merged_chr_CLEAN <- merged %>%
>                             mutate(chr=substring(scaffold, 4)) # Substring start from the 4th character.
>     print(head(merged_chr_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_chr_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_chr_CLEAN))
> 
>     #Separate 'Alleles' into 'Allele 1' and 'Allele 2'
>     cat("\nSeparate 'Alleles' column into 'A' and 'B'.\n")
>     merged_chr_allele_CLEAN <- merged_chr_CLEAN %>%
>                                mutate(
>                                       A=substr(alleles,1,1), #first character
>                                       B=substr(alleles,nchar(alleles),nchar(alleles)) #last character
>                                       ) #mutate
>     print(head(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN))
> 
>     #Create [log10p].
>     cat("\nCreate [log10p].\n")
>     merged_chr_allele_CLEAN$log10p <- merged_chr_allele_CLEAN$log.p/log(10)
> 
>     print(head(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_chr_allele_CLEAN))
> 
>     #Take subset of [merged_chr_allele_CLEAN]
>     merged_CLEAN1 <- merged_chr_allele_CLEAN %>%
>                         subset(select = c("all.data.id", "src", "chr", "position", "assay.name.all", "A", "B", 
>                                           "log.p", "log10p", "effect", "stderr", 
>                                           "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con", 
>                                           "freq.a0", "freq.a1", "freq.b0", "freq.b1",
>                                           "freq.a", "freq.b", "MAF",
>                                           "im.freq.a", "im.freq.b", "avg.rsqr", "min.rsqr", 
>                                           "gt.rate", "gt.freq.a", "gt.freq.b"))
>     #Assign new names
>     colnames(merged_CLEAN1)<-c("all.data.id", "src", "chr", "position", "snpid", "A", "B", 
>                               "log.p", "log10p", "effect", "stderr", 
>                               "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con",
>                               "freq.a0", "freq.a1", "freq.b0", "freq.b1",
>                               "freq.a", "freq.b", "MAF",
>                               "im.freq.a", "im.freq.b", "avg.rsqr", "min.rsqr", 
>                               "gt.rate", "gt.freq.a", "gt.freq.b")
> 
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN1))
> 
>    ##-----------------------------------
>    cat("\nCreate [MAF_old].\n")
>     #Initialize [MAF_old]
>     merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old <- NA
> 
>     cat("\n-Genotyped case ([src == G]).\n")
>     #Genotyped case ([src == G])
>     ##Replace [MAF_old] - genotyped ([src == G])
>     merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old <- ifelse(
>                                 merged_CLEAN1$src == "G",
>                                 pmin(merged_CLEAN1$gt.freq.a, merged_CLEAN1$gt.freq.b),
>                                 merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old  # keep existing values.                            
>                                 ) #ifelse
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN1))
> 
>     # [MAF_old] <- when only genotyped case is considered
>     ## histogram
>     hist(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old)
>     ## summary
>     cat("Max. of [MAF_old]: ", max(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Min. of [MAF_old]: ", min(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Mean. of [MAF_old]: ", mean(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Median. of [MAF_old]: ", median(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Length of non-empty [MAF_old]: ", sum(!is.na(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old)))
> 
>     cat("\n-Imputed case ([src == I]).\n")
>     #Imputed case ([src == I])
>     ##Replace [MAF_old] - Imputed ([src == I])
>     merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old <- ifelse(
>                                 merged_CLEAN1$src == "I",
>                                 pmin(merged_CLEAN1$im.freq.a, merged_CLEAN1$im.freq.b),
>                                 merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old  # keep existing values (e.g., those from src == "G")                            
>                                 ) #ifelse
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN1, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN1))
> 
> 
>     # [MAF_old] <- when both genotyped and imputed cases are considered
>     ## histogram
>     hist(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old)
>     ## summary
>     cat("Max. of [MAF_old]: ", max(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Min. of [MAF_old]: ", min(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Mean. of [MAF_old]: ", mean(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Median. of [MAF_old]: ", median(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Length of non-empty [MAF_old]: ", sum(!is.na(merged_CLEAN1$MAF_old)))
> 
>     #Save the data BEFORE removing SNPs by [MAF_old]
>     cat("\nSave the results in [merged_CLEAN1.txt].\n")
>     #write.table(merged_CLEAN1, file=paste0(dir,"/ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,"/merged_CLEAN1.txt"), sep="\t", quote=F, row.names=F, col.names=T)
>     cat("\n")
>    ##-----------------------------------
> 
> 
>     #Remove SNPs with MAF < 0.01
>     cat("\n-Remove SNPs with MAF < 0.01.\n")
>     merged_CLEAN2 <- merged_CLEAN1 %>%
>                         filter(MAF>=0.01) #Automatically drops rows with MAF = NA as well (since NA >= 0.001 is NA, and filter() drops NA by default)
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN2, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN2, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN2))
> 
>     # [MAF] <- when both genotyped and imputed cases are considered

>     ## histogram
>     hist(temp)
>     ## summary
>     cat("Max. of [MAF]: ", max(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Min. of [MAF]: ", min(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Mean. of [MAF]: ", mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Median. of [MAF]: ", median(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Length of non-empty [MAF]: ", sum(!is.na(temp)))
> 
>     #Take subset of [merged_CLEAN]
>     merged_CLEAN2 <- merged_CLEAN2 %>%
>                         subset(select = c("all.data.id","src",
>                                           "chr", "position", "snpid", "A", "B", 
>                                           "log.p", "log10p", "effect", "stderr", 
>                                           "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con",

>                                           "freq.a", "freq.b", "MAF", "MAF_old"
>                                           ) # select
>                               ) # subset
> 
>     #Save the data AFTER removing SNPs by [MAF]
>     cat("\nSave the results in [merged_CLEAN2.txt].\n")
>     write.table(merged_CLEAN2, file="../output/write_1.txt", sep="\t", quote=F, row.names=F, col.names=T)
>     cat("\n")
> 
>     #Export the data in the global environment

> 
>     cat(paste0("\n*------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*\n"))
>      
>   } #for

> munge_sumstats_subgroups <- function(sub, dir) {
>   for (SUBGROUP in sub) {
>     cat(paste0("\n*----------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP, " --------------------------------*\n"))
> 
>     #read the data
>     merged_CLEAN2 <- get(paste0("merged_CLEAN2_", SUBGROUP))
> 
> 
>     #Keep 'chr1-22' only.
>     cat("\nKeep 'chr1-22' only.\n")
>     merged_CLEAN3_temp <- merged_CLEAN2 %>%
>                         filter(chr %in% as.character(1:22)) # Keep chr1-22 only.
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN3_temp))
> 
> 
>     #Create raw p-value.
>     cat("\nCreate raw p-value.\n")
>     merged_CLEAN3_temp$pval <- exp(merged_CLEAN3_temp$log.p)
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN3_temp))
> 
>     # [pval] <- raw p-value
>     temp <- merged_CLEAN3_temp$pval
>     ## histogram
>     hist(temp)
>     ## summary
>     cat("Max. of [pval]: ", max(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Min. of [pval]: ", min(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Mean. of [pval]: ", mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Median. of [pval]: ", median(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Length of non-empty [pval]: ", sum(!is.na(temp)))
> 
>      # [log.p] <- natural log p
>     temp <- merged_CLEAN3_temp$log.p
>     ## histogram
>     hist(temp)
>     ## summary
>     cat("Max. of [log.p]: ", max(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Min. of [log.p]: ", min(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Mean. of [log.p]: ", mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Median. of [log.p]: ", median(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Length of non-empty [log.p]: ", sum(!is.na(temp)))
> 
>      
>     #Take subset of [merged_CLEAN3_temp].
>     cat("\nTake subset of [merged_CLEAN3_temp].\n")
>     merged_CLEAN3 <- merged_CLEAN3_temp %>%
>                         subset(select = c("chr", "position", "snpid", "A", "B",

>                                           "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con",
>                                           "MAF") #select
>                               ) #subset
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN3, n=5))

>     cat("\n")
>     cat(paste0("\n*------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*\n"))
>       
>  } #for

> metaanalysis_sumstats_subgroups <- function(sub, dir) {
>   for (SUBGROUP in sub) {
>     cat(paste0("\n*----------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP, " --------------------------------*\n"))
> 
>     #read the data
>     merged_CLEAN2 <- get(paste0("merged_CLEAN2_", SUBGROUP))
> 
>     # Create [merged_CLEAN4_temp]
>     merged_CLEAN4_temp <- merged_CLEAN2
>       
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN4_temp, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN4_temp, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN4_temp))
> 
>      #[src]
>      print(table(merged_CLEAN4_temp$src))
>       
>      #[chr]
>      print(table(merged_CLEAN4_temp$chr))
>       
>     #Create raw p-value.
>     cat("\nCreate raw p-value.\n")
>     merged_CLEAN4_temp$pval <- exp(merged_CLEAN4_temp$log.p)
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN4_temp, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN4_temp, n=5))

> extract_h2_summary <- function(file) {
> 
>   lines <- readLines(file)
>   
> # ---- Extract sample name from file path ----
>   if (grepl("ever_tobacco_user_[a-zA-Z]+_h2", file)) {
>     sample <- sub(".*ever_tobacco_user_([a-zA-Z]+)_h2.*", "\\1", file)
>     
>   } else if (grepl("birthyear_bin[0-9]+", file)) {
>     sample <- sub(".*birthyear_bin([0-9]+).*", "bin\\1", file)
>     
>   } else if (grepl("groupingBIN[0-9]+", file)) {
>     sample <- sub(".*groupingBIN([0-9]+).*", "groupingBIN\\1", file)
>     
>   } else {
>     sample <- "full"
>   }
>     
> # ---- Extract LDSC output lines ----
>   h2_line         <- grep("Total Observed scale h2:", lines, value = TRUE)
>   intercept_line  <- grep("^Intercept:", lines, value = TRUE)
>   lambda_line     <- grep("^Lambda GC:", lines, value = TRUE)
>   mean_chi2_line  <- grep("^Mean Chi\\^2:", lines, value = TRUE)
>   ratio_line      <- grep("^Ratio:", lines, value = TRUE)
> 
> # ---- Parse numeric values safely ----
>   h2          <- if (length(h2_line)) as.numeric(sub(".*h2: ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", h2_line)) else NA
>   h2_se       <- if (length(h2_line)) as.numeric(sub(".*\\((.*)\\).*", "\\1", h2_line)) else NA
>   intercept   <- if (length(intercept_line)) as.numeric(sub(".*Intercept: ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", intercept_line)) else NA
>   intercept_se<- if (length(intercept_line)) as.numeric(sub(".*\\((.*)\\).*", "\\1", intercept_line)) else NA
>   lambda_gc   <- if (length(lambda_line)) as.numeric(sub(".*Lambda GC: ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", lambda_line)) else NA
>   mean_chi2   <- if (length(mean_chi2_line)) as.numeric(sub(".*Mean Chi\\^2: ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", mean_chi2_line)) else NA
>   ratio       <- if (length(ratio_line)) as.numeric(sub(".*Ratio: ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", ratio_line)) else NA
> 
> # ---- Return one-row data frame ----
>   data.frame(
>     Sample = sample,
>     h2 = h2,
>     h2_se = h2_se,
>     Intercept = intercept,
>     Intercept_se = intercept_se,
>     Lambda_GC = lambda_gc,
>     Mean_Chi2 = mean_chi2,
>     Ratio = ratio
>   )
> }
> subdirs <- c("ever_tobacco_user")
> log_files <- file.path(results_dir, paste0(subdirs, "_h2_raw.log"))
> heritability_df <- map_dfr(log_files, extract_h2_summary)

> munge_sumstats_subgroups <- function(sub, dir) {
>   for (SUBGROUP in sub) {
>     cat(paste0("\n*----------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP, " --------------------------------*\n"))
> 
>     #read the data
>     merged_CLEAN2 <- get(paste0("merged_CLEAN2_", SUBGROUP))
> 
> 
>     #Keep 'chr1-22' only.
>     cat("\nKeep 'chr1-22' only.\n")
>     merged_CLEAN3_temp <- merged_CLEAN2 %>%
>                         filter(chr %in% as.character(1:22)) # Keep chr1-22 only.
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN3_temp))
> 
> 
>     #Create raw p-value.
>     cat("\nCreate raw p-value.\n")
>     merged_CLEAN3_temp$pval <- exp(merged_CLEAN3_temp$log.p)
> 
>     print(head(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_CLEAN3_temp, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_CLEAN3_temp))
> 
>     # [pval] <- raw p-value

>     ## histogram
>     hist(temp)
>     ## summary
>     cat("Max. of [pval]: ", max(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Min. of [pval]: ", min(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Mean. of [pval]: ", mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Median. of [pval]: ", median(temp, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
>     cat("Length of non-empty [pval]: ", sum(!is.na(temp)))

>     ## summary

> restructure_sumstats_subgroups <- function(sub, dir) {
>   for (SUBGROUP in sub) {
>     cat(paste0("\n*----------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP, " --------------------------------*\n"))
>     data_name <- paste0("sumstats_", SUBGROUP)
>     data_name_new <- paste0("sumstats_", SUBGROUP, "_subset")
> 
>     # keep certain columns in [sumstat_SUBGROUP]
>     cat("\nkeep certain columns in [sumstat_SUBGROUP].\n")
>     assign(data_name_new, subset(get(data_name), select=c("all.data.id", "src", "log.p", "effect", "stderr", 
>                                                           "N_tot", "N_cas", "N_con", "pass",
>                                                           "freq.a0", "freq.a1", "freq.b0", "freq.b1",
>                                                           "freq.a", "freq.b", "MAF")), envir = .GlobalEnv)
>     print(head(get(data_name_new),n=5))
>     print(dim(get(data_name_new)))
>     # remove original data to save space  
>     rm(list = data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
> 
>     # merge [sumstat_SUBGROUP_subset] and [snp_all_merged_subset] using "all.data.id"
>     cat("\nmerge [sumstat_SUBGROUP_subset] and [snp_all_merged_subset] using all.data.id.\n")
>     merged <- merge(get(data_name_new), snp_all_merged_subset, by="all.data.id") # I do not specify "all=T" as I only need the matching SNP.
>     print(head(merged, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged))
> 
>     #Remove 'chr' from 'scaffold'.
>     cat("\nRemove 'chr' from 'scaffold'.\n")
>     merged_chr_CLEAN <- merged %>%
>                             mutate(chr=substring(scaffold, 4)) # Substring start from the 4th character.
>     print(head(merged_chr_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(tail(merged_chr_CLEAN, n=5))
>     print(dim(merged_chr_CLEAN))
>

>                                                                                           # Define:

>

> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> # Create N_cas (=the number of cases used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)

> print(dim(sumstats))

> read_substats_subgroups <- function(subgroup, sumstat_dir) {
> for (SUBGROUP in subgroup) {
> cat(paste0("\n*------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP," ----------------------------------*\n"))
> cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
> 
> cat(paste0("\n1. [ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat]\n"))
> cat("\n")
> cat("1) Read the data.\n")
> sumstats <- fread(paste0(sumstat_dir,"/ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat"), sep="\t", skip=1, header=F)
> cat("-Assign column names.\n")
> colnames(sumstats)<-c("all.data.id", "src", "log.p", "effect", "stderr", "pass", 
>                       "im.num.0", "dose.b.0", "im.num.1", "dose.b.1", 
>                       "AA.0", "AB.0", "BB.0", "AA.1", "AB.1", "BB.1")
> 
>     
> # Create N (=the number of individuals used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_tot <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0
>                                             +sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.0+sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                       NA) #ifelse
>                       ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))    
>     
> # Create N_cas (=the number of cases used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_cas <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                    ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                               NA) #ifelse
>                              ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> # Create N_con (=the number of controls used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_con <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0,

>                               NA) #ifelse

> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")

> read_substats_subgroups <- function(subgroup, sumstat_dir) {
> for (SUBGROUP in subgroup) {
> cat(paste0("\n*------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP," ----------------------------------*\n"))
> cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
> 
> cat(paste0("\n1. [ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat]\n"))
> cat("\n")
> cat("1) Read the data.\n")
> sumstats <- fread(paste0(sumstat_dir,"/ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat"), sep="\t", skip=1, header=F)
> cat("-Assign column names.\n")
> colnames(sumstats)<-c("all.data.id", "src", "log.p", "effect", "stderr", "pass", 
>                       "im.num.0", "dose.b.0", "im.num.1", "dose.b.1", 
>                       "AA.0", "AB.0", "BB.0", "AA.1", "AB.1", "BB.1")
> 
>     
> # Create N (=the number of individuals used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_tot <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0
>                                                 +sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                    ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.0+sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                           NA) #ifelse
>                          ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> # Create N_cas (=the number of cases used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_cas <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                    ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                               NA) #ifelse
>                              ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> # Create N_con (=the number of controls used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_con <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0,
>                    ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.0, 
>                               NA) #ifelse
>                              ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
>     
> #save results
> data_name <- paste0("sumstats_",SUBGROUP)
> assign(data_name, sumstats, envir = .GlobalEnv)
> 
> #print the saved data
> cat(paste0("Return first 5 rows of [",data_name,"]\n"))
> print(head(get(data_name), n=5))
> cat(paste0("Return last 5 rows of [",data_name,"]\n"))
> print(tail(get(data_name), n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(get(data_name)))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(get(data_name)$all.data.id)))
> 
> cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n")
> 
> } #for:SUBGROUP

> read_substats_subgroups <- function(subgroup, sumstat_dir) {
> for (SUBGROUP in subgroup) {
> cat(paste0("\n*------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP," ----------------------------------*\n"))
> cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
> 
> cat(paste0("\n1. [ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat]\n"))
> cat("\n")
> cat("1) Read the data.\n")
> sumstats <- fread(paste0(sumstat_dir,"/ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat"), sep="\t", skip=1, header=F)
> cat("-Assign column names.\n")
> colnames(sumstats)<-c("all.data.id", "src", "log.p", "effect", "stderr", "pass", 
>                       "im.num.0", "dose.b.0", "im.num.1", "dose.b.1", 
>                       "AA.0", "AB.0", "BB.0", "AA.1", "AB.1", "BB.1")
> 
>     
> # Create N (=the number of individuals used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_tot <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0
>                                             +sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.0+sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                       NA) #ifelse
>                       ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> # Create N_cas (=the number of cases used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_cas <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                    ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                               NA) #ifelse
>                              ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> # Create N_con (=the number of controls used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_con <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0,

> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")

> read_substats_subgroups <- function(subgroup, sumstat_dir) {
> for (SUBGROUP in subgroup) {
> cat(paste0("\n*------------------------------- ", SUBGROUP," ----------------------------------*\n"))
> cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
> 
> cat(paste0("\n1. [ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat]\n"))
> cat("\n")
> cat("1) Read the data.\n")
> sumstats <- fread(paste0(sumstat_dir,"/ever_tobacco_user_",SUBGROUP,".dat"), sep="\t", skip=1, header=F)
> cat("-Assign column names.\n")
> colnames(sumstats)<-c("all.data.id", "src", "log.p", "effect", "stderr", "pass", 
>                       "im.num.0", "dose.b.0", "im.num.1", "dose.b.1", 
>                       "AA.0", "AB.0", "BB.0", "AA.1", "AB.1", "BB.1")
> 
>     
> # Create N (=the number of individuals used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_tot <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0
>                                             +sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.0+sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                       NA) #ifelse
>                       ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))    
>     
> # Create N_cas (=the number of cases used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_cas <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.1+sumstats$AB.1+sumstats$BB.1,
>                    ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.1, 
>                               NA) #ifelse
>                              ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> # Create N_con (=the number of controls used to compute the association statistics for each SNP)
> ## Genotyped case ([src]=G) & Imputed case ([src]=I)
> sumstats$N_con <-  ifelse(sumstats$src == "G", sumstats$AA.0+sumstats$AB.0+sumstats$BB.0,
>                    ifelse(sumstats$src == "I", sumstats$im.num.0, 
>                               NA) #ifelse
>                              ) #ifelse
> 
> cat("Return first 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(head(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("Return last 5 rows of [sumstats.txt]\n")
> print(tail(sumstats, n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(sumstats))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(sumstats$all.data.id)))
>     
> 
> #save results
> data_name <- paste0("sumstats_",SUBGROUP)
> assign(data_name, sumstats, envir = .GlobalEnv)
> 
> #print the saved data
> cat(paste0("Return first 5 rows of [",data_name,"]\n"))
> print(head(get(data_name), n=5))
> cat(paste0("Return last 5 rows of [",data_name,"]\n"))
> print(tail(get(data_name), n=5))
> cat("\nSize of a table: (# of rows, # of columns)\n")
> print(dim(get(data_name)))
> cat("\nCount if there are any missing values in 'all.data.id:\n'")
> print(sum(is.na(get(data_name)$all.data.id)))
> 
> cat("\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n")
> 
> } #for:SUBGROUP
> }

Python code

This module also assesses whether the paper’s Python code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 11 Python code files.

Run order

The scripts were ordered by their data dependencies (a script writing a file another reads runs first) and numeric filename prefixes. Python has no source()-equivalent import-based ordering signal (an import loads a module, not the paper’s own analysis flow), so that basis never applies here.

Order File Runs after Basis
1 01_build_meta_locus_inputs.py — numeric
2 01_harmonize_metal_meta.py — numeric
3 02_make_joblists.py — numeric
4 03_extract_locus_sumstats_metal.py — numeric
5 03_susie_completion_qc.py — numeric
6 04_combine_susie_outputs.py — numeric
7 05_summarize_highpip_patterns.py — numeric
8 06_meta_locus_evidence_tables.py — numeric
9 07_exact_variant_overlap.py — numeric
10 08_plot_moderated_maxpip.py — numeric
11 utils.py — none

File paths

Every data path in the code works in the repository as deposited.

Execution

The Python code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 11 scripts: 0 ran without error, 0 errored, 0 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse, and 0 are written for Python 2 and not run. 1 file was not run on its own, because other files import it: utils.py (by 01_build_meta_locus_inputs.py, 04_combine_susie_outputs.py, 05_summarize_highpip_patterns.py, 07_exact_variant_overlap.py, 08_plot_moderated_maxpip.py). Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions (e.g. in a requirements.txt).

Ethics Approval Check

Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

GWAS participants were 23andMe research participants aged 18 or older who provided informed consent for use of their fully de-identified data for research.

Provided informed consent to participate in the 23andMe Research.

Participants are considered related if they share more than 700 centimorgans (cM) of identity-by-descent (IBD), including regions where they share one or both genomic segments IBD.

Because the number of participants genotyped in each five genotyping platforms is very different (>90% of participants were genotyped on v4 or v5), the effective number of samples for each variant can be highly variable.

The 23andMe data was collected in compliance with all applicable laws, from human subjects who provided informed consent under an IRB-approved protocol in accordance with US federal guidelines for Protection of Human Subjects.

Participants provided informed consent and volunteered to participate in the research online, under a protocol approved by the external AAHRPP-accredited Salus IRB (https://www.versiticlinicaltrials.org/about-us/our-brands/salus-irb). 23andMe has complied and will comply with all applicable laws and ethical requirements to protect the identity and privacy of human subjects from whom the data was collected.

Mechanisms of Sex-and GenerationalModeration of SI SI was defined as a binary outcome indicating whether the participant had smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their lifetime.

Ethics approval statement:

The 23andMe data was collected in compliance with all applicable laws, from human subjects who provided informed consent under an IRB-approved protocol in accordance with US federal guidelines for Protection of Human Subjects.

Participants provided informed consent and volunteered to participate in the research online, under a protocol approved by the external AAHRPP-accredited Salus IRB (https://www.versiticlinicaltrials.org/about-us/our-brands/salus-irb). 23andMe has complied and will comply with all applicable laws and ethical requirements to protect the identity and privacy of human subjects from whom the data was collected.

At Purdue University, the following determination was made after IRB review under IRB study number STUDY2026-00001158: “The Purdue Human Research Protection Program (HRPP) Office determined that the proposed activity is not research involving human subjects as defined by DHHS and FDA regulations.”

Power Analysis Check

No power analyses were detected.

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen’s d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.
